name: Amoud Foundation
mission: Founded in 1998, the Amoud Foundation impacts the local and global communities by helping people help themselves through sustainable humanitarian projects while maintaining trusting relationships. Amoud is an international humanitarian organization that today serves the people in the Horn of Africa. Amoud also does work on the home-front including helping with the 2006 Hurricane Relief and 2015 Garland Tornado recovery.

rich_narrative.summary: founded in 1998, Amoud Foundation is a Texas-based humanitarian organization focused on providing direct relief to vulnerable populations in Somalia and Somaliland. The organization operates with a high degree of financial efficiency, reporting <cite id="5">total revenue of $9,535,194</cite> in FY2023. Their mission centers on long-term stability for the most marginalized, specifically supporting <cite id="1">15 orphan centers and two schools</cite> dedicated to children who are deaf or blind. By maintaining a <cite id="1">program expense ratio of 89.3%</cite>, the foundation ensures that the vast majority of donor contributions directly fund its core initiatives, which include water projects, food aid, and healthcare services. This lean operational model is further evidenced by a <cite id="1">fundraising efficiency of $0.00 per $1 raised</cite>, meaning the charity does not spend donor funds on professional fundraising fees. While the organization is smaller than some global relief giants, its <cite id="5">28-year track record</cite> and deep focus on the Horn of Africa provide a specialized avenue for donors seeking to impact that specific region. The foundation is <cite id="2">verified as Zakat-eligible</cite>, allowing Muslim donors to fulfill their religious obligations through programs that serve the poor (fuqara) and needy (masakin).
